about: Semitone's style library: tags you combine (like Suno/Udio style tags) and the profiles behind them. A profile describes musical habits across many songs (chords, tempo, range, rhythm, sound, production), never any single song: no melodies, lyrics, recordings or MIDI are copied, and no voice is imitated. Each 'dna' point carries a confidence (high = sourced, med = some evidence, low = hunch) and sources, in the same shape as STYLE_DNA in web/semitone-studio.html. Wiring: see AGENTS.md, 'Style library and tags'.

tagKinds.label: Genre
tagKinds.help: Sets the core: chords, rhythm, structure.

tagKinds.label: Soundtrack & media
tagKinds.help: The vibe of a score, show, film or game.

tagKinds.label: Composer
tagKinds.help: A composer's writing habits (Orchestral, or Compose for small-ensemble writers).

tagKinds.label: Producer
tagKinds.help: How it's produced: drums, sounds, effects, arrangement tricks. Layers on top of any base.

tagKinds.label: Mood
tagKinds.help: Nudges key, tempo, density and brightness.

tagKinds.label: Era
tagKinds.help: Picks period instruments, drums and mix colour.

tagKinds.label: Your reference
tagKinds.help: A song or album you own, read by the song analyser: only numbers are kept (key, tempo, structure, energy, chords, tonal balance).

blendRules: The first base tag (genre, artist, soundtrack, composer or reference) sets the core profile.

Each further base tag blends in: chord transition weights (m) are averaged with weight 0.35, numbers (bpm, density, leap, register, swing) move 35% towards it, and its DNA points are listed under 'also from'.
A producer tag replaces the production layer (kit, groove, instruments, sound, articulation, mix moves) but never the chords or melody habits. Two producers: the second adds only its mix moves.
Mood, era and instrument tags apply small deltas (below) after blending, clamped to the engine's ranges.
Conflicts are shown, never silently resolved: e.g. Jazz + Trap asks whether the bass walks or plays 808s.
After choosing, a card lists what each tag changed, with Undo. The song is regenerated only when the user presses Use these tags.

accordion.label: Accordion
accordion.needs: a new accordion instrument (not in INSTR yet)

upright-bass.label: Upright bass
upright-bass.needs: a new upright bass instrument (bassgtr is the stand-in)

existingTags.about: The current styles and orchestral templates become tags too, so nothing is lost.

artist.Lana Del Rey: sadcore (or one of artistEras["Lana Del Rey"])

style.name: Camp synth-pop
style.desc: Major-key pop that moves between big four-chord loops (IV–V–I–vi, I–ii–vi–IV, I–vi–IV), two-chord stomps (I–IV) and mixolydian ♭VII–IV–I turns, coloured with added 6ths and 9ths; 80s synths and drums; a theatrical voice that saves its top notes for the chorus.

art.info: Theatrical: accented phrase starts, held top notes with vibrato, short punchy notes in the verse.

arrangement.preChorus: hold the ii chord for the whole pre-chorus
arrangement.drumsTrick: double the beat-four snare every other bar (a Motown take on the backbeat)
extras: pedal steel as an unexpected colour

profiles.mixHint: Wide 80s synth stack, multi-tracked; bright and loud; strings and pedal steel tucked behind.

dna.tagline: camp 80s synth-pop with Broadway-sized hooks
dna.intro: Chappell Roan's songs, produced and co-written by Dan Nigro, pair simple major-key loops with jazzy colours, 80s drums and synths, and a theatrical vocal.

points.t: Across nine songs her harmony is all major-family but varied: IV–V–I–vi (Good Luck, Babe!), I–ii–vi–IV (Pink Pony Club), I–IV (Hot To Go!), I–vi–IV with a vii° (Femininomenon), I–IV–ii–IV with 9ths and 11ths (Casual), IV–I–V and a minor iv (The Subway), and mixolydian ♭VII–IV–I (The Giver, My Kink Is Karma). Tempos run from about 84 to 140 BPM.
points.used: chord matrix from all nine songs, bpm range

points.t: Good Luck, Babe! loops IV–V–I–vi in D major, with an added 6th and 9th on the V and a 9th on the vi for jazzy colour.
The pre-chorus holds a single ii chord and the bridge stays on it too.
The tempo drifts between about 113 and 121 BPM, unusual for modern pop.
80s-sounding drums with a Motown-influenced backbeat (the beat-four snare doubled in alternate bars) and an 80s synth groove.
Verse melodies sit on chord tones with syncopation; chorus phrases open on the highest notes. The delivery is theatrical (Kate Bush and Tori Amos are cited).
Dan Nigro co-writes and produces; he describes building songs around the artist's voice and story.

style.name: Electro dance-pop
style.desc: Mostly minor-key dance-pop around 115–125 BPM: i–VI, i–III–VI, VI–VII–i and i–VII–VI–iv loops, with major-key choruses now and then (I–V–vi–IV); robotic verses, choruses that open up, stutter hooks.

art.info: Clipped, robotic verse lines and accented hooks; the chorus opens into longer notes.

arrangement.hooks: a vocal hook opens the song; a stuttering hook follows the chorus
arrangement.needs: a stutter-edit effect for the post-chorus hook (not in the engine yet)

profiles.mixHint: Clipped marching beat, soaring electronics, dry upfront vocal; synths carry over from section to section.

dna.tagline: minor-key electro dance-pop with stutter hooks
dna.intro: Lady Gaga's early hits with RedOne set dark minor loops at a dance tempo under 80s-inspired synths, with robotic verses and big, clear choruses.

points.t: Across seven songs she leans minor (about 4 in 5 sections): i–III–VI and VI–VII–i (Bad Romance), i–VII–VI–iv (Applause), i–VI and i–III–VI–v (Rain On Me), with major-key choruses in Paparazzi (I–V–vi–IV) and Shallow (ii–V–I).
Just Dance: C♯ minor, 119 BPM, C♯m–E–B–F♯m (i–III–VII–iv), uptempo dance-pop with electropop and synth-pop elements.
Poker Face: G♯ minor, 120 BPM, verse G♯m–E/G♯–F♯, chorus G♯m–E–B–F♯ (i–VI–III–VII), vocal range F♯3–B4.
80s-inspired synths and robotic verses; a vocal hook opens the song and a stuttering hook follows the chorus.
Critics heard clipped marching beats with soaring electronics and a mild R&B flavour.

style.name: 70s soft rock
style.desc: Few chords used three ways: major-key I–V–IV and V–vi–IV loops, and minor two-chord vamps (VI–VII, i–VI) under a hypnotic steady groove; Rhodes and layered guitars, three-part harmonies on every chorus.

art.info: Relaxed, conversational lines; held notes lightly shaped, never belted.

arrangement.harmony: three-part harmony on the chorus, doubled
arrangement.sections: verse, pre-chorus and chorus can share the same chords; change texture instead (a tom accent into the pre-chorus, vibraphone with delay, congas at the back)
arrangement.drums: an 8-bar drum loop feel: steady and hypnotic

profiles.mixHint: Warm 70s tape; guitars spread across the stereo field; congas placed far back; bass simple and droning.

dna.tagline: warm 70s soft rock: few chords, hypnotic grooves, stacked harmonies
dna.intro: On Rumours, Fleetwood Mac built rich records from very few chords: Lindsey Buckingham changed texture, not harmony, to make sections feel different, over steady grooves and three-part harmonies.

points.t: Across six songs: two-chord minor vamps (Dreams VI–VII, Rhiannon i–VI), major loops (Go Your Own Way I–V–IV, Everywhere V–vi–IV, Don't Stop I–IV / I–V–IV, Landslide IV–I–ii), and a switch to the relative minor for a chorus (Go Your Own Way). Mid-tempo songs run about 115–136 BPM.
Dreams began as 'just three chords'; Buckingham made three sections from identical chords that each sound different.
points.used: low chord variety; sections differ by texture

points.t: An eight-bar loop of Mick Fleetwood's drumming gave Dreams its deep, hypnotic effect; the bass is simple and softly droning.
points.used: steady groove, low ghost notes, rootfifth bass

points.t: Three-part harmonies were doubled for a fuller sound; the chorus harmonies came from Buckingham playing triads on piano.
Keyboards across Rumours: Fender Rhodes (the basis of Dreams), Hammond B3, Clavinet, Wurlitzer and grand piano.
Don't Stop uses a triplet snare rhythm into a shuffle; Never Going Back Again uses brushes.

style.name: Funk rock
style.desc: Natural-minor riffs built from jams (i–VI, i–VI–III–VII, i–VII–iv, III–VII–iv–i), with the odd major-key ballad; a busy, melodic bass that knows when to lay out, clean bright guitar, half-rapped verses and sung choruses.

art.info: Rhythmic, half-rapped verse lines full of short notes and ghosted syllables; choruses sing out.

arrangement.bass: melodic and busy, but leaves space so the busy moments stand out (fewer notes, more impact)
arrangement.guitar: clean, raw Strat-into-amp tone; clear single lines and varied textures rather than distortion walls
arrangement.needs: a slap-bass articulation option (not in the engine yet)

profiles.mixHint: Raw, dry and close (recorded in a house); drums live and punchy; little processing.

dna.tagline: jam-born funk rock: melodic bass, clean guitar, rap-sung verses
dna.intro: On Blood Sugar Sex Magik, produced by Rick Rubin, the band moved from funk-metal toward melodic funk rock: Flea played fewer, more melodic notes and John Frusciante favoured clear lines over noise.

points.t: Their hits are mostly natural minor: i–VI and III–VII–iv–i (Californication), i–VI–III–VII and i–v (Otherside), i–VII–iv (Dani California); Under the Bridge is the major-key exception (I–V–vi–iii–IV) with a minor bridge. Tempos about 84–122 BPM.
Californication, Otherside and Snow are four-chord songs; the band and Rick Rubin keep it simple.
Flea cut back the slap technique for melodic bass lines and a minimalist approach: fewer notes so the busy moments stand out.
Frusciante's guitar was less noisy, leaving room for clearer lines and textures, over a raw, unprocessed Strat-and-Marshall tone.
Songs grew from jams; Give It Away came from one. Rick Rubin helped arrange drum beats, guitar melodies and lyrics.
Funk and rap rhythms in the verses, melodic sung choruses.

style.name: Parisian waltz
style.desc: Waltzes and repeating piano figures in minor keys (i–III–v–VII, i–iv–v, iv–VII–i–v), with sudden bright turns to mixolydian or Lydian colour; rippling piano arpeggios, an accordion tune, small toy-like colours.

instr.lead: accordion (needs a new instrument; organ is the stand-in)

art.info: Light and clear: detached waltz notes, the odd grace note, no slides.

arrangement.accompaniment: a repeating piano figure (arpeggios or oom-pah-pah) that never stops
colours: a typewriter or hand-claps as percussion
arrangement.form: the main waltz returns in several versions (piano alone, accordion, full)

profiles.mixHint: Intimate and dry, like a small room; no drums; instruments panned as if around a table.

dna.tagline: merry-go-round waltzes for piano and accordion
dna.intro: Yann Tiersen's Amélie score is built from waltzes and simple repeating patterns, with the accordion giving it its French character and small colours (chimes, mandolin, a typewriter) adding charm.

points.t: Minor-key pieces with simple loops: La Valse d'Amélie iv–VII–i–v–i (in 6/8), Comptine d'un autre été i–III–v–VII, J'y suis jamais allé i–iv–v; La Maison turns to G mixolydian (I–♭VII) and A♭ Lydian (I–II) for bright moments.
The accordion is the most prominent instrument and gives the score its French character.
Waltzes are central: the main theme comes in three versions and waltzes recur, giving a merry-go-round effect.
The piano pieces use simple accompaniment patterns, arpeggios and rippling figures; one is described as Chopinesque.
Colour instruments include mandolins, celeste-like chimes, a music box, hand-claps, a typewriter and ondes Martenot.

songsAnalysed.key: G mixolydian / F# minor / Ab lydian

style.name: Analog synth score
style.desc: Warm analog synths: the main title rocks between a major-7th I chord and iii at 84 BPM under a running arpeggio; slow pulse, dissonance to build dread, few or no drums.

art.info: A synth lead: long tones and slow glides, no vocal-style ornaments.

arrangement.ostinato: an arpeggiated synth pattern runs through each cue
arrangement.build: layers enter one at a time; intense scenes 'go even harder'

profiles.mixHint: Warm and 70s-sounding rather than cold digital 80s; depth and slow movement, never harsh.

dna.tagline: warm analog synth dread, Carpenter-style
dna.intro: Kyle Dixon and Michael Stein of the band Survive scored Stranger Things on analog synths; the show was pitched to them as John Carpenter meets Italian giallo and Giorgio Moroder.

points.t: The main title is in C major at 84 BPM, alternating a major-7th I chord with iii (with an added 13th).
points.used: mode ionian, key C, bpm 84, I↔iii matrix

points.t: Analog synths throughout; Stein's SH-101 is on nearly every record, plus kit-built modular gear.
The show's sound was pitched as John Carpenter, Italian giallo and Giorgio Moroder; Carpenter's use of dissonance to drive scenes is a cited influence.
They prefer warm, 70s-style recording to cold digital 80s sounds, aiming for depth and movement rather than harshness.
Arpeggiated synth patterns are a signature of the main theme.

dna.note: Only the main title is analysed; other cues may differ. Add more cues to data/progressions.json and re-run tools/build_style_matrices.py.

style.name: Swing jazz
style.desc: ii–V–I progressions with sevenths and extensions, a walking bass, swung eighths, a ride-cymbal groove and comping chords off the beat.

profiles.groove: swing (new: ride-cymbal pattern, hi-hat on 2 and 4, feathered kick)

instr.bass: upright bass (needs a new instrument; bassgtr is the stand-in)

art.info: Swung phrasing with scoops, falls and ghosted notes; accents on the off-beats.

profiles.form: 32-bar AABA (A = 8 bars) is the default; also 12-bar blues. Sections are named A, A, B (bridge), A, then solo choruses over the same form.
engineNeeds: a 'swing' groove (ride pattern, hi-hat on 2 and 4)
chord extensions on every chord by default (7, 9, 13) and tritone substitution in the suggestion engine (SUGSTYLE tri already exists)
the AABA and 12-bar blues forms in the structure list
improvised solo choruses: a melody generator that varies the head over the form

Bossa nova.needs: a bossa groove and nylon-guitar comping pattern

profiles.mixHint: Small-room acoustic sound: piano centre, bass close, drums with lots of ride and brushes; little compression.

dna.tagline: swing: ii–V–I, walking bass, ride cymbal
dna.intro: Classic small-group jazz runs on ii–V–I progressions with seventh chords, a walking bass line on every beat, swung eighth notes and a ride-cymbal groove, usually in 32-bar AABA or 12-bar blues forms.

points.t: ii–V–I progressions are extremely common in jazz and imply passing key centres; Honeysuckle Rose goes back and forth between ii and V before resolving, and Satin Doll is built on them.
In minor the ii is half-diminished (iiø7–V7–i); the V7 can be swapped for ♭II7 (tritone substitution) for chromatic root motion.
points.used: minor matrix; tri weight 0.8 in Chord ideas

points.t: Autumn Leaves in G minor: a ii–V–I into the relative major (Cm7–F7–B♭maj7), E♭maj7 as a link, then the minor ii–V–i (Am7♭5–D7–Gm); 32 bars in swing.
points.used: circle-of-fifths motion in the minor matrix, form

points.t: Fly Me to the Moon is a 32-bar ABAC swing tune; Autumn Leaves is AABC.
The Girl from Ipanema (bossa nova) opens on an added-9th I chord and moves to II7 (V7 of V) and ♭VII.
Walking bass: one note per beat, chord tones on strong beats, passing tones into the next root. Swing eighths long–short, ride cymbal and hi-hat on 2 and 4 keep time.

style.name: Brat club-pop
style.desc: Loud minimal club-pop that slips between major and minor: IV–V–I–vi and V–vi–IV loops, minor i–v–iv–III and VI–III–iv–i, and two-chord vamps that never name their key; unusual voicings, a morphing bit-crushed synth, sudden silences and stutters, Auto-Tuned vocals.

art.info: Talk-sung, clipped lines with Auto-Tune polish: almost no vibrato, accented hooks.

arrangement.process: start from a loop and build structure by muting and deleting (subtraction)
arrangement.silence: drop the music out where a downbeat is expected (a sudden gap, maybe just claps)
arrangement.stutter: copy and repeat a 16th note of vocal for a stutter
arrangement.voicings: stacked fourths and close clashes (a minor second inside a chord)
arrangement.harmony: hint at two or three keys without settling; a raised 4th can tint a major chorus Lydian
needs: a vocal Auto-Tune effect for the guide vocal
random filter cutoff per chord on the lead synth

profiles.mixHint: 'Very loud and bold' minimalism: few parts, all huge; bit-crushed, formant-filtered saw synths; dry, upfront, Auto-Tuned vocal.

dna.tagline: loud minimal club-pop that never quite names its key
dna.intro: On Brat, Charli XCX and producers including A. G. Cook made what she called 'a unique minimalism that is very loud and bold': club-pop rooted in 2000s English rave, built from loops by subtraction, with Auto-Tuned vocals and ambiguous harmony.

points.t: Across eight songs she moves between major loops (Boom Clap IV–V–I–vi, Apple V–vi–IV, Track 10 ii–iii–IV–V–vi) and minor ones (B2B i–v–iv–III, Speed Drive VI–III–iv–i, 360 v–VI), about 64% major-family sections; tempos about 92–173 BPM.
Genres listed as electropop, synth-pop, club-pop, hyperpop, dance and electroclash; drawn from the London rave scene and 2000s English rave music.
She described the sound as 'a unique minimalism that is very loud and bold'; more aggressive and club-oriented than Crash.

360 hints at C major, F major and A minor without settling; I Think About It All The Time uses simple chords with unusual voicings (stacked fourths, a minor-second clash); Sympathy Is a Knife's chorus has a raised 4th (Lydian colour).
points.used: chord matrix (A minor / C / F / G), voicings, borrow weight

points.t: Built in Logic with Serum synths, starting from loops and shaping structure by muting and deleting; abrupt silences replace expected downbeats; a stutter is made by repeating a 16th note of vocal.
A morphing lead: saw wave into a formant filter with the cutoff randomised on each chord, then a low-pass and bit-crushing distortion.
points.used: lead synth (needs random cutoff per chord)

points.t: Charli records melodies with real-time Auto-Tune in her headphones; songs are likely improvised straight into the computer.

songsAnalysed.song: I Think About It All The Time

style.name: Lana Del Rey · Born to Die / Paradise (2012)
style.desc: Minor loops (♭VI–i–♭VII, i–VII–VI) and a few bright major songs, over slow hip-hop and trip-hop beats with big orchestral strings; a low, close vocal that jumps up for the chorus.

art.info: Low and close in the verse, a jump to a lighter, higher voice in the chorus; long held notes with vibrato and sighing fall-offs.

arrangement.drums: slow hip-hop beat: heavy kick, snare on 3, sparse hats; drums drop out for the intro and first verse
arrangement.strings: big string section doubling the chord loop, swelling into each chorus
arrangement.voice: verse an octave below the chorus

profiles.mixHint: Strings wide and loud, beat dry and punchy in the middle, vocal close and up front with a long plate reverb.

dna.tagline: hip-hop beats under Hollywood strings
dna.intro: The first era: Born to Die and the Paradise EP. Producers mixed orchestral strings with hip-hop and trip-hop beats.
stats: mostly 66–112 BPM, a few up to 144
mostly minor loops, some bright major songs

points.t: Born to Die, Blue Jeans, National Anthem and Summertime Sadness loop ♭VI–i–♭VII-type minor progressions; Radio, American and Bel Air are bright major songs.
Baroque and orchestral pop with trip-hop and hip-hop beats; strings arranged by Larry Gold.
Paradise (Rick Nowels, Rick Rubin) is slower and darker, with glacial strings and mellotron.
Chords for ten songs come from guitar chord sites, not Hooktheory: tune with the song analyser.

style.name: Lana Del Rey · Ultraviolence (2014)
style.desc: A psychedelic guitar record: a live band in slow motion, heavy reverb electric guitars, minor vamps (i–VII–VI) and mixolydian I–♭VII–IV, choruses that slow down instead of lifting.

instr.lead: reverb electric guitar (needs a new instrument; steel guitar with long reverb is the stand-in)

art.info: Sung live with the band: relaxed, a little behind the beat, smoky low notes, fall-offs at phrase ends.

arrangement.band: a live band playing together: drums, bass, two electric guitars, organ; little editing
arrangement.chorusTrick: West Coast-style: the chorus drops to a slower tempo instead of getting bigger (needs a tempo change per section)
arrangement.solos: long reverb-soaked guitar solos and outros
extras: strings only on a few songs

profiles.mixHint: Warm and roomy, like a band in one room: guitars drenched in reverb and tremolo, drums soft and natural, vocal slightly back in the mix.

dna.tagline: psychedelic desert rock in slow motion
dna.intro: Produced by Dan Auerbach with a live band, Ultraviolence trades the beats and strings for reverb-heavy electric guitars.

points.t: Psychedelic rock, dream pop and desert rock; recorded with a seven-piece live band and vocals sung live.
West Coast's chorus drops from about 123 to 100 BPM.
Ultraviolence and Shades of Cool move between D minor and F major, with a guitar solo section.
Chords for six songs come from guitar chord sites: tune with the song analyser.

style.name: Lana Del Rey · Honeymoon (2015)
style.desc: The most cinematic era: slow minor songs (i–VI, i–VI–iv–V) with swirling strings, jazz colours and saxophone, sometimes over trap hi-hats and 808; old-Hollywood and spy-film moods.

instr.lead: tenor saxophone (needs a new instrument; prolead is the stand-in)

art.info: Slow and languid: very long notes, wide vibrato, glides between notes, nothing accented.

arrangement.strings: full string section carries the song; harp and celesta glitter on top
arrangement.drums: often no drums; otherwise slow trap hi-hats and 808 under the strings (High by the Beach, Art Deco)
arrangement.jazz: saxophone or jazz-drum colour on some songs (Terrence Loves You, Art Deco)

profiles.mixHint: Huge, slow string reverb; vocal soft and close with long delays; 808 low and round when it appears.

dna.tagline: old-Hollywood strings, jazz smoke and slow 808s
dna.intro: Honeymoon, produced with Rick Nowels and Kieron Menzies, is slow, orchestral and cinematic, with jazz and trap touches.

points.t: Baroque pop, dream pop, jazz and trip hop, with trap beats on some songs; orchestral strings and saxophone.
Honeymoon (the song) sits on i–VI in F minor at about 77 BPM; Salvatore uses an augmented chord between i and VI.
Chords for ten songs come from one album chord chart: tune with the song analyser.

style.name: Lana Del Rey · Norman Fucking Rockwell! (2019)
style.desc: 70s soft rock and piano ballads: major and mixolydian keys (I–v–IV, I–♭VII–vi), Laurel Canyon guitars, mellotron and long psychedelic jams with guitar solos.

art.info: Conversational and warm; more of her middle voice, light vibrato, long held endings.

arrangement.jams: some songs stretch into long instrumental jams and guitar solos (Venice Bitch, The Greatest)

profiles.mixHint: Warm 70s tape sound: soft drums, piano and acoustic guitar close, mellotron and strings behind, a little tape saturation.

dna.tagline: Laurel Canyon soft rock with psychedelic jams
dna.intro: Produced with Jack Antonoff and Rick Nowels, NFR leans on piano, 70s soft rock and folk rock, with long psychedelic passages.
stats: major and mixolydian, a few minor songs

points.t: Soft rock and folk rock with psychedelia; produced mostly with Jack Antonoff and Rick Nowels.
Venice Bitch moves between G mixolydian and A minor and stretches into a long jam.
The Next Best American Record and Love Song move between a major key and its relative minor.
Chords for nine songs come from guitar chord sites: tune with the song analyser.

style.name: Lana Del Rey · Blue Banisters (2021)
style.desc: Piano-led Americana and folk with jazz-band horns: mostly major keys (I–iii–vi–IV, I–ii–IV), songs that change tempo and mood midway, intimate and unpolished.

instr.lead: brass and pedal steel (need new instruments; organ is the stand-in)

art.info: Close and diary-like: plain middle-voice lines, little vibrato, phrases that run on.

arrangement.piano: solo piano carries most songs; band joins late or not at all
arrangement.tempo: some songs change tempo and mood midway (Text Book, Black Bathing Suit)

profiles.mixHint: Dry and close: piano in the room, vocal very close with little reverb, horns and strings natural.

dna.tagline: piano diaries with Americana and jazz horns
dna.intro: Blue Banisters, made with several producers, is piano-led, folky and jazzy, and less polished than NFR.

points.t: Americana, folk, jazz and pop; piano-led with strings, horns, pedal steel, Mellotron and Rhodes.
Text Book and Black Bathing Suit change key and tempo between sections (Black Bathing Suit goes from 83 to 153 BPM in the pre-chorus).
Chords for nine songs come from guitar chord sites: tune with the song analyser.

songsAnalysed.song: If You Lie Down with Me

style.name: Cinematic
style.desc: Slow minor themes that circle i–VI–III–VII (Time, Now We Are Free), Lydian and chromatic-mediant colour shifts, an ostinato that builds over a long crescendo: piano and strings first, then percussion, brass and choir.

art.info: Long legato lines, swelling with expression; ostinatos short and even.

arrangement.form: three acts: sparse setup (piano, pad), escalation (ostinato, percussion, swelling strings), climax (brass, choir, full percussion, sub hits); silence before the biggest hit
arrangement.ostinato: a repeating 8th-note figure (strings or piano) under the theme, as in Time and The Rock
arrangement.harmony: circle a few minor chords; colour shifts like I→iv, i→IV, I→II, and VImaj7–v–i–v7 (Interstellar)

profiles.mixHint: Huge hall reverb, wide strings, low end from sub hits not bass; dynamics automated over minutes.

dna.tagline: a slow theme that grows into a wall of sound
dna.intro: Film-score and trailer writing for songs: Zimmer, Richter, Einaudi themes and Bond-style ballads.

points.t: Zimmer's Time loops iv–i–III–VII at 63 BPM; Now We Are Free circles i–VI–VII; Richter's On the Nature of Daylight moves i–v–III–VI–VII.
Signature film moves: I→iv (Leia), i→IV (Binary Sun), I→II (E.T.), VImaj7–v–i–v7 (Interstellar), I–♭VI–IV (Man of Steel).
Trailer cues follow three acts: sparse setup, escalation with rhythmic motifs, climax with brass, choir and sub drops; silence before the biggest hit.

base: long hall reverb
strings swell by expression
risers and reverse swells into each act
silence before the climax hit

byEmotion.melancholy: solo piano and strings only, no percussion
byEmotion.triumphant: brass and choir climax, key lift
byEmotion.tense: ostinato and low strings, dissonant held notes, sub drops
byEmotion.hopeful: major lift (i→IV or I→II) at the climax

style.name: Country
style.desc: Major-key songwriting (I–IV–V, I–V–vi–IV, I–vi) with a few minor story songs (Jolene, Before He Cheats); acoustic and Telecaster guitars, pedal steel answering the vocal, sparse verses and full choruses.

art.info: Story-first: clear words, scoops and small cracks into notes, slides on leaps.

dna.tagline: hyperpop: pitched-up vocals, sugary synths, exaggerated pop
dna.intro: A. G. Cook founded PC Music, whose sound (later called hyperpop) takes 1990s and 2000s pop to surreal extremes: pitched-up, chopped vocals, sugary synths, grime sub-bass and sudden shifts. He is Charli XCX's longtime executive producer.

points.t: Vocals heavily processed, usually pitched up or chopped into rhythmic elements; bright, sugary, artificial-sounding synths.
Big synth blasts and high vocals recall Eurodance and happy hardcore; grime-style sub-bass anchors the low end.
points.used: kit electro, groove fourfloor, bass probass

points.t: Abrupt changes in timbre and rhythm; stacked discordant layers; glossy polish deliberately overstated; dissonant inversions give a sinister edge.
Influences include K-pop and J-pop and the production of Max Martin and Jimmy Jam & Terry Lewis.
Charli XCX's longtime executive producer, credited on Brat.

pass.name: Hyperpop
pass.summary: Familiar pop made glossy to the point of exaggeration: bright synthetic sounds, vocals chopped into rhythms, abrupt mutes and switches, odd chord voicings under a bright surface.
pass.firstListen: Listens to every single sound on its own: is this kick, this synth patch, as characterful as it could be?
asks: Is it Brat? If an idea is boring, move on.
Which pop cliché could be pushed further?

template.name: Dark fantasy saga
template.mood: A cello-led theme over a driving string riff, minor and major traded back and forth, octave doublings that grow with every repeat.

sections.name: Riff
sections.lesson: A string riff states the rhythm that drives the whole cue. Trading C minor for C major (the parallel key) keeps you unsure whether the story is hopeful or doomed.
sections.roles: violins II and violas: riff (ostinato); cellos and basses: root; timpani: soft pulse

sections.name: Theme A
sections.lesson: The cello carries the theme: wide range and a dark sound. The harmony walks i–v–♭VII–iv before coming home. The second violins keep the riff going so the sections stay linked.
sections.roles: cellos: melody; violins II: riff; violas/horns: harmony; basses: bass

sections.name: Theme B
sections.lesson: Starting on ♭VI instead of i gives a sense of adventure. Big leaps (octaves) and turning the theme's shape upside down make it new.
sections.roles: violins I + cellos in octaves: melody; horns: counter; low brass: bass

sections.name: Climax
sections.lesson: The theme returns an octave higher with the full orchestra: Djawadi raises the melody by an octave on repeats to add drama.
sections.roles: violins I/II + cellos: melody in octaves; brass: harmony and hits; percussion: drive

sections.name: Coda
sections.lesson: Back to the riff alone, still swapping minor and major, ending on minor.

variants.Player-piano covers: A Westworld-style option: re-arrange the user's own song as a solo player piano or string quartet cover. Only the user's own songs, never other people's.

dna.tagline: cello themes, string riffs, minor/major tension
dna.intro: Ramin Djawadi's Game of Thrones theme switches between C minor and C major, uses a driving riff shared by the second violins, and puts the cello up front.

points.t: Opens on C minor for two bars, then C major (the parallel key); the A section moves i–v–♭VII–iv; the B section starts on ♭VI.
The cello was chosen as the main instrument for its range and dark sound (the show's creators banned pianos and flutes).
A riff drives the piece and the second violin shares it in later sections; contour inversions, octave leaps and raising the melody an octave on repeats are recurring devices.
Influences include Beethoven, Brahms, Tchaikovsky and 80s rock, especially Metallica.

For Westworld he moved from Game of Thrones' dramatic sound to a more minimal, classic one built on piano (including an old western-style piano), with piano covers of rock songs such as Black Hole Sun and Paint It Black.
points.used: a 'Minimal piano' variant (user's own songs only for covers)

points.t: Westworld's score features player-piano style covers of rock songs.
Tempo and exact meter of the main title not confirmed from a source; set as a starting point.

soundtrackLibrary.about: Media you can pick as a tag. Each maps to a profile, a blend of tags, or both; the user sees it as one tag. Add more by the same pattern; anything without a researched profile is a blend of existing tags and is labelled 'approximate'.

referenceTag.about: 'Use a song or album as the style'. Two routes: (1) the song analyser reads audio files the user owns, on their computer, and saves only numbers (key, mode, tempo, section lengths, energy curve, chord-change statistics, loudness and tonal balance) as a private profile named after the file; nothing from the recording itself is stored or shared. Several files (an album) are averaged. (2) Typing a title that isn't in the library: offer the closest tags (genre, mood, era, instrument) for the user to confirm; if the built-in assistant (AGENTS.md idea 24) is approved later, it can draft a profile for review.

existingStyles.about: Chord habits for the original styles, rebuilt from many songs. Apply to STYLES in web/semitone-studio.html by id: m (for the style mode), mMajor, mMinor, modeShare. Keep each style mode; modeShare lets a new song switch family.

songs: all the good girls go to hell

artistEras.about: Artists whose albums sound very different get one profile per era. Picking the artist tag shows the eras as chips; with none picked, Semitone uses the artist's default profile. Picking one era uses only that era's chords, tempo, sounds and mix. Picking two or more blends them by the normal blend rules (first is the core). Eras are never mixed silently. A song tag ("piano", "cinematic") can also narrow the songs used: the matrix is rebuilt from only the matching songs in data/catalog.json, if at least 4 match.

producerPass.about: A producer pass runs on a finished song: Semitone proposes what that producer would likely do, as session notes. Each move is one line with a reason and its own on/off switch; A/B compares your version and the pass while it plays; the pass is one undo step and so is each move. "How far" picks the levels: sounds & mix (sound, mix) / + arrangement (arrangement, structure) / + writing (writing: only these touch melody or chords, and say so). "Try another take" draws a different subset and variant of the moves. Wording is always "<name>-style pass, based on how they are known to work": never quotes or first-person lines in the producer's voice. op strings are a small action language for the engine (mute, muteDoubles, cutBars, dropDrums, drumFeel, tempoCurve, layer, layerRamp, thin, swapSound, kit, groove, fx, vocalTake, addSection, melodyRepeat, melodyMatch, chordColor); moves the engine cannot do yet stay listed but greyed with "coming soon". Each pass also has firstListen (what the pass looks at first, said about the producer, never in their voice) and asks (questions the card puts to the user). Moves carry c (confidence) and src; onByDefault=false moves are offered but start switched off. The pass also reads the song's emotion and vibe: data/sound-library.json emotionRules give the baseline, the producer's fxStyle.byEmotion says how that producer handles it, and sound moves suggest real instruments (sound-library instruments) with software options and the user's own presets when found.

genreVariants.about: A genre can offer variants (like artist eras): picked as chips under the genre tag. A variant only overrides the fields in "set".
